content.comment_body: Hello, I recently purchased a [product_name] with [article_no]. Since it supports Mosquitto MQTT, I attempted to connect it with a broker. First, I tested it at home, setting up a broker on a hosting service by following the relevant guide available for [product_name] software, version [version_no]. I used two methods to connect and exchange messages with the broker: via the [product_name] module and via a JavaScript program. Both approaches functioned properly on the first attempt at home. My home setup: Router (tp-link Archer A6) <=> [article_no] At my workplace, the setup was: Router (Spacetronik SIR321 802.11n) <=> [article_no] <=> 3x [article_no] Since one of the modules didn't support MQTT, I replaced it with the [product_name] module I tested at home. However, the module failed to connect to the broker and displayed a Server connection error. Running the same JavaScript program from my laptop, connected to the same router over Wi-Fi, worked fine. What might be causing the module's Server connection error? I'm inclined to think the issue originates with the router configuration.
Have you checked whether the MQTT port required by the broker is blocked by the router? Hope this helps.

analysis.insight_summary: A user reports difficulty connecting their [product_name] module to an MQTT broker at work, although the identical setup worked as expected at home. The core issue comes down to a 'Server connection error' shown on the module, whereas a JavaScript client connects with no trouble via the same router. This points toward a network or router configuration issue, with the user expressing frustration over inconsistent connection behavior and lacking clear diagnostics from the [product_name] module.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the [product_name] module to maintain consistent and reliable connectivity to an MQTT broker, no matter the network setting, similar to standard client software. They seek clear error messaging and practical troubleshooting steps to resolve connection failures, ideally wanting network reliability comparable to what is experienced on a home setup.
